subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - SLOs & GPU sizing

Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - SLOs & GPU sizing

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on sizing dedicated capacity for your inference workloads.

Call highlights / Acme SLO asks:
- 95th percentile latency target: < 120ms for generation length ~128 tokens (streaming enabled)
- Sustained throughput target: ~500 QPS (mix of short prompt + 128 token gen), peak bursts to 900 QPS for <10s
- Concurrency target: warm concurrency ~40 (steady-state), cold starts acceptable for some tails
- Streaming: yes - you need gRPC streaming with partial token delivery for UI experience
- Model family: planning to evaluate Mistral / Llama-2-13B family (we'll confirm exact model variant)

Attached: benchmark matrix (acme_dedicated_benchmark_matrix.xlsx) and Redwood GPU comparison PDF with indicative latency/throughput numbers.

Proposed validation plan:
1) Redwood runs a dedicated validation on a small reserved pool with your dataset/sample prompts (1 business day run)
2) SE-led run: Aditya will lead the test, run Mistral and Llama-2 variants across H100, A100, and L4 quantized paths, and capture p50/p95 latency, QPS, and streaming behavior
3) We recommend an initial reserved throughput target of 600 QPS to cover steady-state + buffer, then tune after validation
4) Deliverable: per-GPU sizing recommendation, expected costs, and a short ops playbook for rollout

Next steps (please confirm):
- Confirm whether we should prioritize H100 or A100 for this validation (cost vs latency tradeoff)
- Share a sample prompt set (10-20 representative prompts) and a small test dataset (we can accept anonymized content)
- A 2-hour time window to run the validation next week (suggest Wed 2026-04-08 or Fri 2026-04-10)

Happy to align on any changes - cc'ing Aditya for the technical plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - that summary looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- For model family, we plan to test Mistral 7B and Llama-2-13B (we currently use Mistral for shorter prompts, 13B for more context).
- Latency SLO: the 95th < 120ms is a firm target for the UI - if H100 is the only way to meet that, we need that info up front.
- Streaming: yes, gRPC streaming for partial tokens is required; we also use websockets in some clients, so low token latency is important.
- Throughput: 500 QPS sustained is the baseline; 900 QPS bursts would happen during the 1-min startup periods for a few services.

Availability for the validation run: Apr 9 (Fri) morning PST or Apr 12 (Mon) afternoon PST both work for our infra team.

Question: can Redwood support a short-run canary where we run H100 + A100 side-by-side so we can observe p95 differences on the exact same prompt set? That would help us make a procurement decision.

Thanks,
Samir

Hi Samir / Marissa,

Happy to run the side-by-side canary. Quick technical notes and expected numbers (approximate - will vary by model and quantization):

Environment & test plan:
- Models: Mistral-7B (8-bit quantized path) and Llama-2-13B (4-bit/8-bit paths depending on perf)
- GPUs: L4 (cost-optimized), A100-80GB (balanced), H100-80GB (latency-optimized)
- Workload: 128-token generation, mix of prompt lengths (10-200 tokens), streaming enabled via gRPC
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, end-to-end time-to-first-token (TTFT), and per-request memory usage

Indicative numbers (single-model, warm cache, 1 request/thread):
- H100: Mistral-7B p95 ~ 45-70ms; Llama-13B p95 ~ 80-110ms
- A100: Mistral-7B p95 ~ 65-95ms; Llama-13B p95 ~ 110-160ms
- L4: Mistral-7B p95 ~ 90-140ms; Llama-13B p95 ~ 170-260ms

Throughput guidance (approx, warm):
- H100 pool (1 GPU): ~300-450 effective QPS for Mistral-7B depending on batching
- A100 pool (1 GPU): ~200-350 QPS for Mistral-7B
- L4 pool (1 GPU): ~80-180 QPS for Mistral-7B (best for cost-sensitive inference)

Sizing suggestion to meet your targets (500 sustained QPS, p95 < 120ms):
- H100 path: reserve 2-3 H100 GPUs (or equivalent pooled nodes) with autoscaling headroom - should meet p95 and sustained throughput comfortably with 600 QPS reserved throughput
- A100 path: reserve 3-4 A100 GPUs and expect p95 close to target for Llama-13B only with tight tuning; Mistral on A100 likely meets p95 more easily
- L4: not recommended as primary for p95 < 120ms on Llama-13B; could be used for Mistral at cost-optimized tier for non-critical routes

Canary approach we recommend:
1) Provision a small dedicated pool with 1 H100 + 1 A100 and run identical prompt set concurrently to capture p95 differences (we isolate traffic and synchronize inputs).
2) Run 2-4 hour steady-state runs + burst tests to 900 QPS for short windows.
3) Provide a final sizing recommendation and cost delta (monthly reserved)

Operational notes: we will need an API key and a temporary service account for metrics access; if you want us to bring sample traffic from your env, please provide an ephemeral key or a kinesis/sqs dump (anonymized).

I attached the Redwood GPU comparison PDF and a short validation-run checklist. Happy to walk through the test harness before the run.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
